MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 24, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director;
  Richard Mollica, Flaming Director; Susan Duenas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBouX,
  Public Works Director; Gail Karish, Deputy City Attorney; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; Tracey Rossine, Environmental Programs
  Manager; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; and Brandie Ayala, Administrative Analyst

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Lloyd Ahern led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettij ohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on June
  17, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda.

  The Council discussed the motion.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM l  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 24, 2024
  Page 2 of 14

David Orszag discussed repairs needed at the Adamson House and other
construction projects in the City. He stated more sand was needed at the entrance
to Zuma Beach and the bathrooms needed to be opened.

Keith Canter stated his property on Sea Star Drive had not been issued a certificate
of occupancy for his property due to litigation from a neighbor over a second-story
ADU. He requested the City issue a conditional certificate of occupancy to occupy
the main level of the home.

Hal Dale deferred time to Craig Gold.

Hassan Soltani deferred time to Craig Gold.

Parisa Soltani deferred time to Craig Gold.

Craig Gold discussed the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority
(MRCA) directing members of the public to access the Escondido Canyon Park
trail using Via Escondido Drive while Winding Way underwent payment repairs.
He stated neighbors were not notified of the change. He stated there is no final
judgement in the legal case between MRCA and Sycamore Park. He discussed the
City’s Mission Statement and zoning regulations. He discussed MRCA’s
installation of a turnstile and signage near Via Escondido. He discussed Resolution
No. 16-19.

Liz Robinson discussed fire and medical response to MRCA’s property on Via
Escondido yesterday. She requested the City review the trail camera footage.

Cheryl Calvert requested help with MRCA and its employees. She discussed the
fire and medical response on Via Escondido yesterday.

Howard Rudzki commended Michel Shane for his work on the 21 Miles in Malibu
film. He commended the City representatives who spoke in favor of the speed
camera bill in Sacramento. He discussed Sycamore Park and the rules in the Local
Coastal Program (LCP).

Robert Stephens deferred time to Elizabeth Stephens.

Bill Einzig deferred time to Elizabeth Stephens.

Kim Calvert deferred time to Elizabeth Stephens.

Elizabeth Stephens discussed safety issues in Sycamore Park and dangers to the
public using Via Escondido Drive as a trail. She discussed traffic on Pacific Coast
Highway (PCH). She requested the City enforce the LCP, LIP and Zoning codes
on MRCA. She stated foot traffic has been open on Winding Way during the paving
project.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 24, 2024
  Page 3 of 14

  Craig Cullen requested members of the public who supported Sycamore Park stand
  up.

  Ryan Embree discussed the temporary use permit (TUP) approved for an event on
  July 4, 2024 at Nobu. He expressed concern about the use of PCH for the event.
  He stated the use of PCH required an encroachment permit from Caltrans. He
  discussed the closed session performance evaluation for the City Manager and the
  number of open code enforcement cases. He discussed the Malibu Inn Motel
  application.

  Nichole McGinley discussed overflowing trash cans at Zuma Beach and asked who
  could address that issue.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary stated Zuma Beach was owned and managed by Los
  Angeles County Beaches and Harbors and he would pass along the complaint about
  overflowing trash cans. He stated the new parking enforcement team would be
  staffed by mid-July and would be providing enforcement for the July 4, 2024
  weekend. He announced SB 1297 had been approved by the Assembly
  Transportation Committee and would be considered by the Assembly Privacy and
  Consumer Protection Committee next. He thanked Bridget Thompson and Michel
  Shane for speaking at the Transportation Committee meeting. He announced a
  community launch event on June 27, 2024 for the PCH safety awareness campaign
  Cruise Malibu: Surf, Sand, Slow. He announced community workshops for
  Caltrans’ PCH master plan feasibility study on July ll, 2024 at City Hall, and July
  18, 2024, Virtually. He stated Caltrans would present on the feasibility study at a
  joint Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission meeting. He stated
  the outreach events for the Malibu Community Lands project had been completed
  and the survey would go live next week. He stated the Community Lands Phase 2
  outreach would begin in August, and the final report would be presented at the
  second meeting in October. He stated dates had been identified for Malibu Film
  society events in July, August, and September. He congratulated Malibu Canyon
  Village for becoming the fourth Firewise community in the City. He stated he
  attended a school district separation mediation meeting last week and planned to
  attend another meeting next week. He announced the City Council Reorganization
  on July 8, 2024. He discussed a tax ballot initiative and stated the California
  Supreme Court had ruled to remote the measure from the November ballot. He
  announced minimum wage in the City was increasing to $17.27 on July 1, 2024.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department, discussed
  events during the last weekend and stated search and rescue performed four rescues
  within four hours. He stated Los Angeles County Lifeguard performed 380 ocean
  rescues, provide medical aid to 436 people, and took 2,700 preventative actions.
  He discussed heavy traffic in Malibu over the weekend. He thanked the City for
  supporting the speed camera bill. He encouraged the public to attend the launch
  event for the Cruise Malibu: Surf, Sand, Slow campaign.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 24, 2024
  Page 4 of 14

  Interim City Attorney Rusin discussed MRCA, public access to Escondido Canyon
  Park using Winding Way, and MRCA’s actions on Via Escondido. He stated staff
  would send a letter to the MRCA and Code Enforcement was gathering information
  related to MRCA’s actions on Via Escondido. He stated the Sheriffs Department
  had been informed regarding MRCA’s actions on Via Escondido and potential
  public safety issues.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated he did
  not know the details of the service call referenced by members of the public.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Stewart, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the letter
  would be shared with the public after it was sent and it would address a number of
  1ssues.

  In response to Mayor Uhring, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated all code
  enforcement action started with a notice and an attempt to obtain compliance.

  ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended a Clean Power Alliance (CPA) retreat,
  a school district separation mediation meeting, and the graduation and promotion
  ceremonies for Malibu Middle School (MMS) and Malibu High School (MHS).
  She stated she received calls from Via Escondido residents and discussed code
  enforcement procedures.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, City Manager McClary confirmed the
  demographic information collected by the flash vote survey for the Community
  Lands proj ect would be used to confirm the reach of the survey in the community.

  Councilmember Riggins discussed the street sweeping RFP and expressed concern
  there was sand on Westward Beach Road and Birdview Avenue impeding traffic.
  She requested staff contact Los Angeles County Beaches and Harbor regarding
  complaints of overflows restrooms at Zuma Beach. She stated she had received
  complaints of plants in right-of-way blocking traffic on Wildlife Rd.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Planning Director Mollica discussed Mr.
  Canter’s property and stated the ADU on second floor was approved via CDP.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she hoped staff could work with the property owner.

  Councilmember Silverstein stated he believed the City could do more than send a
Vi
  letter to MRCA. He stated the Council could not take action on this issue because
  it was not on the agenda. He requested consensus to add an item to the next agenda.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item at the July 8, 2024
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 24, 2024
  Page 5 of 14

Regular meeting to discuss MRCA’s recent actions on Via Escondido and related
issues.

Councilmember Silverstein discussed clapping in public meetings and Mayor Pro
Tem Stewarts’ comments about clapping. He stated Sycamore Park was not
designed to be a public thoroughfare. He addressed Mr. Canter and stated he hoped
staff could work with him. He discussed a letter received from Adrian Fernandez.

Councilmember Grisanti stated personnel matters should not be discussed in open
ses31on.

Interim Attomey Rusin recommended against discussing personnel matters or
items not on the agenda.

Mayor Uhring stated the letter had been posted on the internet.

Councilmember Silverstein discussed the June 24, 2024 letter from Adrian
Fernandez and the allegations in the letter. He requested consensus to bring back
an item to direct the City to commission an independent investigation into the
matter and into favoritism of certain developers by staff.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart requested guidance from the City Attorney.

Councilmember Grisanti expressed opposition to the item at this time.

Mayor Uhring indicated support for the item.  He stated this issue would be
discussed during the election.

Interim City Attorney Rusin stated staff and legal counsel would meet to discuss
the letter tomorrow and would provide an update to Council.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart discussed the human resources regulations regarding
harassment claims in California.

In response to Mayor Uhring, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated staff from the City
Manager’s Office, Human Resources, City Attorney’s Office, and employment
attorneys planned to participate in the meeting.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated he
would provide a confidential update to the Councilmembers.

Councilmember Silverstein encouraged staffto work with Michel Shane on his safe
driving education campaign.‘

In response to Councilmember Silverstein, City Manager McClary stated staff
continued to meet with Mr. Shane.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 24, 2024
  Page 6 of 14

Councilmember Silverstein discussed the limited p001 hours for sports programs
and discussed the request for qualifications (RFQ) process for the swim program.

In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated staff worked with the Parks and Recreation Commission on the RFQ for a
swim program. She stated staff had identified panelists to review the applications
and make a recommendation. She stated staff planned to work with the Parks and
Recreation Commission Ad Hoe Committee to select the final vendor.

Councilmember Silverstein requested the swim program agreement be approved by
the Council.

Community Services Director Riesgo stated staff anticipated entering into a
contract by July for the Fall season and bringing the item back to Council would
cause delays.

Councilmember Silverstein expressed that he found it preferable to allow the two
swim programs to continue operating in the Fall to allow for a more public process.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated the water polo program was expected to restart in the Fall and would limit
the available pool hours.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart suggested bringing back the swim program contract at the
first meeting in August. He discussed the City Council’s Rules of Procedure and
Decorum and how clapping can impact public meetings. He stated Meril May had
submitted photos of the overflowing trash cans at Zuma Beach to Supervisor
Horvath and it was being responded to. He stated sending a letter was the beginning
of the process to address the issues with MRCA. He stated he attended the
community land outreach meeting at the Malibu West Clubhouse. He discussed
renaming of the MHS theater for Dick Van Dyke and discussed the Malibu
Education Foundation (MEF) and Shark Fund fundraising. He requested MEF
provide an update on how the funding from the City had been used. He requested
the fire brigades provide an update on how they are using their funding. He thanked
Michel Shane and Bridget Thompson for testifying on speed camera bill and
discussed the hearing before the Assembly Transportation Committee. He stated
four axel trucks were not allowed on PCH except for deliveries, and asked the
Sheriffs Department and California Highway Patrol (CHP) to enforce the
prohibition of four axel trucks. He stated he looked forward to the parking
enforcement team. He discussed traffic near SoHo House and Nobu.

Councilmember Silverstein commended Mayor Pro Tem Stewart for. his work on
the speed camera bill.

Mayor Uhring expressed disappointment that the City did not take action sooner to
address MRCA on Via Escondido.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 24, 2024
  Page 7 of 14

  In response to Mayor Uhring, City Manager McClary stated staff was working on
  a memo to Council on changes to Flaming staff reports.

  Mayor Uhring discussed the TUP for the July 4, 2024 event at Nobu. He indicated
  support for an update from the new MEF board.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart suggested bringing back an update at the first meeting in
  August.

  City Manager McClary stated staff would reach out to MEF.

  Mayor Uhring discussed his first two years on the Council and the Mayor rotation.
  He commended Councilmember Silverstein for his work as the Mayor. He
  discussed Councilmember Grisanti’s letter to the editor in The Malibu Times.

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended the MHS and MMS graduation and
  promotion ceremonies with Councilmember Riggins. He stated he attended the
  SM-MUSD bond feasibility study group with Mayor Uhring. He stated he attended
  renaming event for the Dick Van Dyke theater at MHS. He stated he attended the
  emergency preparedness fair at Corral Canyon. He stated he met with an individual
  who wanted to do an email program on traffic safety. He stated he attended a school
  district separation meeting and the Special City Council meeting. He commended
  Meril May for reporting the overflowing trash cans at Zuma Beach. He inquired
  how much funding was needed for the repairs at Adamson house. He stated he
  received pictures of the activities in Sycamore Park and he was glad the City was
  taking action.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item Nos. 3.B.9. was pulled by the public. Item Nos. 3.B.4., 3.B.6. and 3.B.7. were

  ITEM 4  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

SUB SITUTUE MOTION
  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Uhring seconded a motion to: l)

  The Council discussed the motions on the floor and directed questions to staff.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved to make a friendly amendment to Councilmember
  Riggins’s motion to: l) adopt Resolution No. 24—31 adopting the Annual Budget
  for Fiscal Year (FY) 2024—25; 2) adopt Resolution No. 24-32 establishing the
  Appropriations Limit for FY 2024-25; and 3) adopt Resolution No. 24-33

  The Council discussed the motion.

  The maker and the seconder accepted the amendment.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 3-2, Councilmember Silverstein
  and Mayor Uhring opposed.

  The Council discussed reserves.
